timeline.desc: With almost continuous rainy days, Milford Sound is home to many temporary and permanent waterfalls. The largest permanent fall is the famous Lady Bowen Falls, located at the southeast end of the sound, north of the wharf. menu.name: World of Deer
menu.desc: Opened in Sept 2018. Museum on the history of deer in NZ and deer antler carvings. Also has a shop selling deer products including carvings and food supplements, but not meat. Some of the carving is done in China.

menu.name: Coronet Peak Night Ski (Wed & Fri only - your Friday is 28 Aug)
menu.desc: Floodlit skiing 4pm to 9pm, Wednesdays and Fridays through to 4 September 2026. The one thing in Queenstown that adds usable hours to an August day rather than losing them to the 18:12 sunset. Only Day 1 of your trip qualifies.

menu.name: The Bathhouse Cafe (Queenstown Gardens)
menu.desc: Your Queenstown breakfast pick. A 1911 bathhouse on the beach at Queenstown Gardens - note this is the CAFE, not the Bathhouse spa on Brecon St.

menu.name: Coronet Peak sightseeing - gondola, toboggan, Heidi's Hut
menu.desc: The Peak Gondola to the summit and back, the designated snowplay and toboggan area, and Heidi's Hut - a small cosy restaurant with an indoor fire.

menu.name: Glenorchy township & the red boatshed
menu.desc: The end of the road, 46 km and about an hour from town. The red boatshed on the wharf is the photograph; Mrs Woolly's General Store is the coffee and the shelter.

menu.name: Gibbston Valley Winery & Wine Cave
menu.desc: New Zealand's largest underground wine cave, in the Gibbston valley 25 min from town on the way to the Kawarau bungy bridge. Indoor, open year round, and a genuine wet-weather answer to a cancelled outdoor day.

menu.name: Gibbston Hop-On Hop-Off Wine Tour (someone else drives)
menu.desc: A shuttle loop between Gibbston cellar doors at your own pace. The best wet-weather answer in the whole region: cellar doors are indoors with fires going, and nobody has to stay sober to drive. Booked through Civitatis/Queenstown Wine Trail.

menu.name: Lord of the Rings filming locations tour
menu.desc: Four hours around the filming sites, most of them within 40 min of town. Runs in most weather because the stops are short.

menu.name: Ayrburn
menu.desc: Your winery pick. A restored 1860s farm precinct between Arrowtown and Lake Hayes with several venues on one site - all indoors with fires, so it holds up whatever the weather. Five minutes from Arrowtown, 25 from town.

menu.name: Coronet Peak afternoon pass (12:30-16:00)
menu.price: Afternoon pass ~NZ$95-135 + rental NZ$65 + outerwear NZ$45 (est)
menu.desc: Half-day access from 12:30 to 16:00, built for late starters. Cheaper than a full day and it leaves the morning free - which is what makes the group split work.

menu.name: Luge
menu.price: Gondola only NZ$69 - with 3 luge rides NZ$99 - unlimited luge NZ$140 (2026)
menu.desc: Skyline gondola up Bob's Peak then the luge track. Five minutes from Fergburger. Gondola only NZ$69, NZ$99 with 3 luge rides, NZ$140 unlimited. Closes in high wind or heavy snow - check the day's status before driving up.

menu.name: The Gibbston Tavern
menu.desc: Wood-fired pizza and craft beer in the middle of the wine valley. The unpretentious stop on a wine day.

menu.name: Sundeck Rooftop Bar
menu.desc: Your rooftop drinks pick. Outdoor, so it wants the good-weather evening - Monday or Tuesday, not Wednesday.

menu.name: Puzzling World
menu.price: Tumbling Towers: free, Great Maze: $18/12, Illusions: $18/14, Combined: $22.50/16
menu.desc: Its major feature is the Great Maze, a 1.5km two-story maze of confusing passages. It also features dozens of optical illusion rooms and a large puzzle centre, cafe and gift shop. Check out Wanaka's version of the Leaning Tower and the incredible Roman toilets.

menu.name: Te Anau-au Caves
menu.desc: A boat trip and guided tour into the Aurora Caves system by walking path and small boats within the cave itself where you will see thousands of glow worms. The caves are only accessible by boat, and Real Journeys operates a quality catamaran for a 30-minute cruise each way. You'll spend approximatel

menu.name: Skyline Gondola
menu.price: $69 adult return; $99 with 3 luge rides; $140 with unlimited luge (2026)
menu.desc: The steepest cable car lift in the Southern Hemisphere, up Bob's Peak for the postcard view over Lake Wakatipu and The Remarkables. Winter sunsets from the top are the reason to time this late - but check the last gondola down.

menu.name: Botswana Butchery
menu.desc: A great restaurant with ambience, sensational service. The menu is extensive and specialises in meat. The whole leg of lamb for 2 could feed 3! The wine list is very good. Prices are at the higher end but sensational for a special occasion. Smaller private room dinning opportunities as well as a gre

menu.name: Milford Sound coach & cruise (guided, from Queenstown)
menu.price: NZ$136-219 per adult (2026); winter rates run 20-35% below summer
menu.desc: The same 13-hour day as self-driving, except somebody else does the 9 hours behind the wheel. In winter the Milford Road can require chains and the drive is genuinely arduous; tour drivers carry them and are trained for it. For a 3-day trip with only one spare day, this is the version that does not

menu.name: The Bathhouse Spa (35 Brecon St)
menu.desc: A European-style bathhouse, not a massage spa: 38, 34 and 12 degree pools, Finnish sauna, scented steam room, two infrared saunas and a tea lounge, self-serve at your own pace. Open to 21:30, so it works after a day on the mountain. BOOKINGS REQUIRED - they do not take walk-ins.

menu.name: Lady Bowen Falls
menu.desc: With almost continuous rainy days, Milford Sound is home to many temporary and permanent waterfalls. The largest permanent fall is the famous Lady Bowen Falls, located at the southeast end of the sound, north of the wharf. Named after the wife of Sir George Bowen, one of New Zealand's earliest gover

menu.name: Stirling Falls
menu.desc: Created by glaciers situated behind the mountains, Stirling Falls is the second largest permanent waterfall, located on the north side of Milford Sound, dropping 146 metres. Some ships are able to get underneath the falling water, making the falls one of the great highlights of the Sound.

menu.name: Coronet Peak Ski Area
menu.price: Afternoon pass NZ$135 + rental NZ$65 + jacket & pants NZ$45 = NZ$245 all in (your research)
menu.desc: The closest field to town, ~25 min from Goldfield Heights. Season 13 Jun to 4 Oct 2026 and late August is the best coverage of the year. Budget roughly NZ$230-290 a head all in: pass, gear and outerwear. Rental prices are the operator's own research.

menu.name: Te Anau Bird Sanctuary
menu.desc: A short walk from downtown, the Te Anau Bird Sanctuary provides the unique opportunity to view some of New Zealand's rarest endangered birds. Be sure to see the takahē, a large flightless bird with beautiful blue plumage and an enormous red beak. With only about 500 takahē left in the world, this is

menu.name: Milford Sound nature cruise (2 hours)
menu.desc: The actual reason to go: out under Mitre Peak to the Tasman Sea and back, past Stirling and Bowen Falls. Rain makes it better, not worse - the walls run with hundreds of temporary waterfalls.

menu.name: Kinross Cellar Door
menu.desc: Five small Central Otago producers pouring under one roof, with a fire going in winter. Easy to combine with Gibbston Valley and Arrowtown in one loop.

menu.name: Glenorchy & Paradise scenic day trip (guided)
menu.desc: The Glenorchy road is the best short drive in the country. Guided means you watch it instead of watching the road - worth it on a wet day when the surface is greasy.

menu.name: Jack's Point Golf Course
menu.desc: Your golf pick. Spectacular, and your own note flags the catch: not much in the way of food options on site, so eat before or after.

menu.name: Bennett's Bluff Lookout
menu.desc: The stop on the Glenorchy road - Pigeon and Pig Islands below, the Humboldts across the water. Roughly 35 min from town. In heavy rain the cloud sits low on the range, which is its own kind of good.

menu.name: Glenorchy Lagoon boardwalk
menu.desc: A flat 30-40 min loop on boardwalk behind the township, through wetland with the Humboldts as a backdrop. Easy underfoot even wet.

menu.name: Paradise & Diamond Lake
menu.desc: Twenty minutes beyond Glenorchy on UNSEALED road with fords. Spectacular, and the first thing to drop in heavy rain - check your rental agreement covers unsealed roads before you commit.

menu.name: Nevis Bungy
menu.desc: New Zealand's highest bungy at 134 m. The bungy is 45 min east of Queenstown; shuttles depart are from the AJ Hackett office on the corner of Shotover St and Camp St in central Queenstown.

menu.name: Harris Mountains Heliski
menu.desc: Harris mountains heliski can be booked from retail stores in Wanaka, and offers a number of different payment options, for a few runs or many. Go when the snow is good or go when the snow is ordinary, and trust your guide and pilot to find a stash. If you book only a few runs and want to do more, th

menu.name: Kawarau Bridge Bungy
menu.price: PRICE UNVERIFIED - the $205 figure is from a 2017 listing and is certainly low now
menu.desc: The 43-metre (141 ft) bungy jump off the Kawarau Suspension Bridge is the world's oldest commercial bungy jump, and the only bungy jump in Queenstown offering tandem jumps.

menu.name: Shotover Jet
menu.desc: Jet boat through the Shotover Canyons at speed, 10 min from town at Arthurs Point. Runs year round - it is cold in August, and they supply the layers.

menu.name: Lake Te Anau
menu.desc: "The cave of swirling water", it is the second-largest lake by surface area in New Zealand (after Lake Taupo) and the largest in the South Island. North Fiord, Middle Fiord and South Fiord are the only inland NZ fiords.

menu.name: The Boatshed Cafe (Frankton)
menu.desc: Your Frankton breakfast pick, and the closest of the three to Goldfield Heights - about 5 minutes.

menu.name: Wolf Coffee Roasters (Arrowtown)
menu.desc: Your Arrowtown breakfast pick. Five minutes from Ayrburn, so it pairs with a Tuesday out that way.

menu.name: Sunfire
menu.price: NZ$80-90 pp; ~NZ$40 if you order light
menu.desc: Your oyster pick. Seafood-led.

menu.name: Blue Kanu
menu.desc: Asian fusion, Polynesian-tiki room. Your easiest booking of the four, and the best fit for all seven.

menu.name: Scroggin Bakehouse (Wanaka)
menu.desc: Your Wanaka pick - the tiramisu danish. Only relevant if you take the Wanaka day option.

menu.name: Fergburger
menu.desc: Your lunch pick. Shortest queue before noon or after 9pm.

menu.name: Wilson Bay lookout
menu.desc: First proper pull-off on the Glenorchy road, right on the lake edge. Two minutes out of the car.

menu.name: Milford Deep Underwater Observatory
menu.desc: This place can only be reached via one of the cruises. What they are trying to do is interesting, but they charge a lot to see the place and you get a whopping 15 minutes total there. There is not even enough time to look through the displays.

menu.name: HeliWorks
menu.desc: Exciting scenic flights in & around Queenstown & Milford Sound, Lord of the Rings flights with the pilots who filmed the trilogy.

menu.name: Winnies
menu.desc: Later in the evenings this pizza bar turns into a popular drinking spot. Dining, drinking and partying under the sun and stars with an opening roof.

menu.name: Lakes District Museum
menu.desc: The museum is also the town's major Information Centre. It is the focal point for all that is the history of the town and the surrounding areas.

menu.name: Arrowtown Chinese Settlement
menu.desc: Historic gold mining huts from the 1880s with informative information; a short walk from the west end of Buckingham Street.

menu.name: Warbirds & Wheels
menu.desc: A museum of classic and vintage automobiles and motorcycles, and war planes, including an A-4 Skyhawk, a Strikemaster, a Vampire, and a Hurricane. It replaced the Fighter Pilots Museum.

menu.name: National Transport & Toy Museum
menu.hours: Daily (except 25 Dec) 8.30am-5pm with extended hours in summer
menu.desc: Has aircraft, cars, trucks, motorcycles, fire appliances, military vehicles and tractors, clockwork and battery powered toys, porcelain dolls, teddy bears, pedal cars and money boxes.

menu.name: Skydive Lake Wanaka
menu.desc: It’s not every day that you strap yourself to a beautiful stranger and leap from a perfectly good aircraft! High altitude tandem skydive. Freefall from 15,000 feet

menu.name: Bullock Bar
menu.desc: A bar with some real Central Otago character, featuring some unique entertainment including indoor ice curling and occasionally sheep racing

menu.name: Queenstown Gardens
menu.desc: Jutting out into Lake Wakatipu, these botanical gardens contain a variety of exotic and native trees and plants as well as a large pond and a range of facilities.

menu.name: Mitre Peak
menu.desc: Rising 1,692 metres, Mitre Peak is Milford Sound's most famous iconic attraction. The mountain is named for its distinctive shape, similar to the mitre headwear worn by Christian bishops.

menu.name: Queenstown Arts Centre
menu.desc: Contemporary art exhibitions and artists studios. Has some paintings for sale.

menu.name: The Ledge Bungy
menu.desc: 47-m drop. Bungy or swing.

menu.name: The Cow Restaurant
menu.desc: Pizza & spaghetti house

menu.name: The Lone Star
menu.desc: Tex-mex, casual dining
Polished restaurant/bar in a circa-1876 stone-built courthouse offering upscale pub grub & a deck.

menu.name: Cruise Milford NZ
menu.desc: Specializes in operating smaller boats. Personal and informative crew.

menu.name: Mitre Peak Cruises
menu.desc: Has smaller launches that get close to the shoreline.

menu.name: Patagonia Chocolates
menu.desc: Boutique chocolate producers with a cafe offering coffees and sweet treats.

menu.name: Arrowtown Bakery
menu.desc: Fantastic pies and other assorted baked goods

menu.name: St. Paul's Angican Church
menu.desc: Wooden church built in 1871.

menu.name: Warbirds Over Wanaka
menu.desc: An air show held every second Easter long weekend. The next show is on 3 - 5 April 2026. See over 50 aircraft from the biplanes of WWI, the stars of WWII, the Korea fighters and the jets of Vietnam. Also military vehicles and Harley Davidson motor cycles.

menu.name: Deep Canyon
menu.desc: Descend the spectacular canyons of the Matukituki valley. Explore crystal pools and native forest. Plunge down water polished chutes, abseil down waterfalls. Climb, swim and float through a spectacular world of water sculpted rock and sparkling, crashing waterfalls.

menu.name: Night n' Day
menu.desc: Hot food and groceries, also at 48 Shotover St.

menu.name: Postmasters
menu.desc: Fine dining

menu.name: Cruise Te Anau
menu.desc: A boutique cruise to the South Fiord of Lake Te Anau and a gentle bush/nature walk to discover the Hidden Lakes.

menu.name: Kepler Track
menu.desc: This track starts from near Te Anau, and the section around the lake to Brod Bay and back makes a pleasant gentle day walk. The complete track ( a circular route) usually takes 3 or 4 days and climbs to 1470 m. Connections from Te Anau by bus or water taxi (to Brod Bay) are available in summer.

menu.name: Routeburn Track
menu.desc: A walking track, part of the Great Walks. There are 4 huts on the track, but you may complete the walk in 3 days. Book the huts a few months in advance - booking opens in May or June. The two ends of the track are apart by road, so travel needs to be planned.

menu.name: Lake Marian
menu.desc: Off Hollyford Road on the way to Milford lies one of the most beautiful places on earth.

menu.name: Loco
menu.desc: Big backpacker bar popular with tour bus groups. Drink specials and theme parties nightly. Not the place for a quiet drink.

menu.name: Destination Queenstown
menu.desc: Visitor information and brochures.

menu.name: The Warehouse
menu.desc: Budget department store.

menu.name: Fergburger
menu.desc: Legendary, large burgers, insanely busy most of the day.

menu.name: At Thai
menu.desc: Thai cuisine

menu.name: The World Bar
menu.desc: Funky, multilevel bar featuring a menu of burgers & pub grub, plus craft beers & teapot cocktails.

menu.name: Southern Discoveries
menu.desc: Runs more cruises, geared towards scenery, wildlife or both.

ideas.name: Nine holes, or a bucket at the range
ideas.why: Half a day rather than a full one, and Jack's Point is the spectacular option at NZ$275 for 18. Queenstown Golf Club on the Kelvin Heights peninsula is the easy nine; Arrowtown Golf Club is the cheap and cheerful one.

ideas.name: The Devil's Staircase drive
ideas.why: SH6 south along the lake toward Kingston - the road is cut into the cliff above Lake Wakatipu and the pull-offs are the point. About 40 min each way to Kingston. Check road conditions first in winter; it is exposed and it ices.

ideas.name: Queenstown - Arrowtown - Wanaka loop over the Crown Range
ideas.why: The big one: the Crown Range is the highest sealed road in New Zealand, and the loop takes 4-6 hours with stops. In late August it can require chains and it closes in snow - check before committing, and have the Kawarau Gorge as the flat-road alternative back.

ideas.name: Gibbston wine valley - cheese and wine
ideas.why: Twenty-five minutes out, all indoors, and the underground wine cave is the best wet-weather hour in the region. Pairs with the Kawarau bungy bridge next door if anyone wants to watch rather than jump.
